correctness.rationale: Commuting idempotents are simultaneously diagonalizable over every F_q because x(x−1) is separable even in characteristic two. Orthogonal products EF, E(I−F),(I−E)F,(I−E)(I−F) decompose the vector space into dimensions t,r−t,s−t,n−r−s+t. Transitive GL_n action and block stabilizer give C=|GL_n|/Π|GL_block|. For n=4m,r=s=2m,t=m+j the exact stratum ratio is q^(−4j²) φ_m^4/(φ_(m+j)^2 φ_(m−j)^2), dominated by a constant times q^(−4j²), establishing total variation by dominated convergence on Z. Count rank-half idempotents and use |GL_k|=q^(k²)φ_k to get q^(4m²) P(commuting)→Θ_q/Φ_q. Independent enumeration of every small prime-field idempotent and ordered pair reproduced all rank strata for (n,q)=(2,2),(3,2),(2,3). This is not an infinite-field/counting proof.
residual_risks: Uniformly random means uniform over all idempotent matrices of fixed rank, not uniform over images alone.
The asymptotic requires q fixed and n=4m; no growing-field or other rank-density limit is stated.

value.rationale: Finite-field projection pairs form a canonical family with a strong commutativity rarity phenomenon. The exact conditioned product-rank distribution and theta normalizing constant give nontrivial asymptotic fluctuations and rare-event probability in a natural matrix ensemble; they are not merely a single finite table.
residual_risks: The finite four-block orbit count itself is classical; value rests on the total-variation limit and sharp rare-commutativity constant.

final_claim: For fixed finite field order q, independent uniform rank-2m idempotents in M_(4m)(F_q), conditioned on commuting, have rank(EF)−m converging in total variation to P(Z=j)=q^(−4j²)/Θ_q; the commutativity probability is asymptotic to q^(−4m²) Θ_q/Φ_q. An exact four-eigenspace formula counts all ordered fixed-rank commuting pairs.
limitations: q is a fixed prime power and both idempotents have exactly half ambient rank; growth is through 4m dimensions.
Individual finite enumeration runs only over prime fields n≤3; analytic proof covers arbitrary q and all m.
